title: Donor-complementary prime editing enables precise kilobase and library-compatible DNA insertions - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Fudan University researchers developed DoPE (donor-complementary prime editing), a one-step, double-strand-break-free method combining a 3'-overhang DNA donor with paired overhang-complementary prime editing guide RNAs and a PE2* prime editor to precisely insert DNA fragments up to 12.5 kb, enable library-scale saturation mutagenesis, and correct diverse disease-causing PRKCSH mutations without recombinases or transposases; the team is filing patents on the method.

insights.claim: DoPE (donor-complementary prime editing) combines a 3'-overhang double-stranded DNA donor with a pair of overhang-complementary prime editing guide RNAs (opegRNAs) and a PE2* prime editor to achieve precise, one-step genomic DNA insertion.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A new DSB-free insertion primitive that could be licensed into gene-editing therapeutics platforms competing with HDR- and recombinase-based large-insertion tools.
insights.quote: donor-complementary prime editing (DoPE), which combines a 3′-overhang double-stranded DNA (odsDNA) donor with a pair of overhang-complementary prime editing guide RNAs (opegRNAs) and a PE2* prime editor

insights.claim: DoPE requires no recombinases or transposases and avoids double-strand breaks entirely, distinguishing it from CRISPR nuclease-based insertion methods and recombinase-dependent platforms that need a pre-installed landing pad.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Positions DoPE as a safety-differentiated alternative to DSB-dependent or multi-step landing-pad insertion methods used by other gene-editing programs.
insights.quote: a one-step, DSB-free and library-compatible method for precise insertion of large DNA fragments without requiring recombinases or transposases

insights.claim: DoPE achieves precise insertion of DNA sequences up to 12.5 kilobases in length, a size range typically requiring recombinase- or nuclease-assisted strategies.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Kilobase-scale, DSB-free insertion capability is directly relevant to gene-replacement and safe-harbor transgene therapeutic programs that need to deliver full coding sequences.

insights.claim: Using short (~30-nucleotide) overhangs, DoPE supports a wide range of insertion sizes, from small fragments to sequences exceeding 10 kb, with a single design framework.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A single short-overhang design rule that scales across payload sizes simplifies adoption versus methods requiring size-specific engineering.

insights.claim: A single opegRNA pair combined with donor pools built from synthesized single-stranded oligonucleotides enabled in situ saturation mutagenesis across a targeted EGFP region at both amino-acid and nucleotide resolution.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Library compatibility positions DoPE as a candidate infrastructure tool for large-scale variant-effect mapping (e.g., variant-of-uncertain-significance classification), a workflow currently dominated by HDR-based saturation genome editing.

insights.claim: DoPE replaced mutant exons of the PRKCSH gene, either individually or simultaneously, to correct diverse mutations, establishing a mutation-agnostic approach that corrected distinct alleles uniformly in vitro.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A mutation-agnostic exon-replacement strategy is attractive for genetic diseases with high allelic heterogeneity, since one therapeutic design could correct many different patient mutations rather than requiring a bespoke fix per variant.
insights.quote: we replace mutant exons of PRKCSH, either individually or simultaneously, to correct diverse mutations, establishing a mutation-agnostic approach that corrects distinct alleles uniformly in vitro

insights.claim: The Fudan University research team behind DoPE is preparing patent applications related to the method, and lead/corresponding authorship is held by Lingbo Wang and Feng Zhang, with data and plasmids available only pending a completed material transfer agreement.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Active patent filing on a foundational gene-insertion method signals intent to license or spin out DoPE into therapeutic or tool-company applications rather than leave it fully open.
insights.quote: The authors are preparing patent applications related to the DoPE method. The authors declare no other competing interests.
